title: Brahmacharya
one_line: Establishing the mind in the supreme Brahman without allowing it to wander — not merely the retention of vital fluid or unmarried student life.
points: Guruji asks whether brahmacharya is merely the retention of vital fluid or unmarried student life, and answers that becoming one with the supreme Brahman alone is brahmacharya.

Our Shrutis and Smritis speak of eight types of obstacles to brahmacharya, given in a verse Guruji quotes: remembering, celebrating, amorous play, viewing, infatuated discussion, planning, determination, and the effort of one who has no partner — 'the wise declare these to be the eight limbs of romantic activity.'

Guruji writes that maintaining brahmacharya today is difficult because of theaters, pleasure houses, restaurants, and similar attractions, but that a man can still achieve some degree of it by avoiding vulgar company, crowded recreation, vulgar books, theaters and restaurants, and secret conversation with strangers of the opposite sex.
Guruji quotes the Bhagavad Gita (xvi:24): the sacred teaching (shastra) is one's measure of what is to be done and not done, and one should act according to what the shastra says.

Guruji writes that a householder does not lose brahmacharya through seminal loss by itself; in the truest sense, the householder alone can attain brahmacharya, citing a mantra that those who engage in romantic activity daily dissipate their energy, while those who delight when desire is in decline engage in true brahmacharya.

Guruji states plainly that if a man has intercourse with his wife during the daytime, his vitality is lost and death will conquer him quickly; he calls the argument that intercourse with other women is therefore acceptable the reasoning of 'perverted rationalists,' and states that intercourse with other women is always forbidden and harmful to brahmacharya even in thought.

According to the shastrakaras Guruji cites, sexual intercourse only at night and in accordance with the menstrual cycle allows even householders to be regarded as brahmacharis; for yogis, day and night are determined not by sunrise and sunset but by which nostril — surya nadi (right) or chandra nadi (left) — the breath moves through, with intercourse permitted only when the breath moves through the chandra nadi at night.

Guruji writes that the interval between the fourth and sixteenth day of a woman's menstrual cycle is the correct time for intercourse according to scriptural experts; beyond the sixteenth day, on new and full moon days, and on other specified days, intercourse is not related to brahmacharya, and union with one's lawful wife should be for the sake of begetting good progeny only.
Guruji describes the promise made upon entering the householder stage: to do nothing apart from one's lawful wife with respect to dharma, artha, and kama.

Veerya (vitality) is described as the transformation of the thirty-second drop of blood into dhatu (semen); preserving the strength of the mind and sense organs requires preserving dhatu, and if it is lost, the strength of the mind and sense organs is also lost.

Guruji concludes that whether working, sleeping, eating, playing, or enjoying intercourse with one's wife, one should think of the Supreme Self at all times; if the mind is thus given to constant thought of the Supreme Self, its strength increases, and this strength is brahmacharya.
In truth, Guruji writes, establishing the mind in the supreme Brahman, without allowing it to wander here and there, is brahmacharya.

sutra.translation: Upon being established in brahmacharya, there is the attainment of vital energy.

quotes: This is only the question of perverted rationalists.
